items.title: GCC chief condemns Houthi attack on KAFD, calls for international action

items.summary: RIYADH — Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Secretary General Jasem Albudaiwi condemned in the strongest terms the treacherous terrorist attack carried out by the Houthi militia against one of the towers in the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) in Riyadh. “The attack constitutes a blatant violation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and a dangerous escalation, reflecting the militia's continued threats to civilian lives, targeting of civilian facilities, and efforts to undermine regional security and stability,” he said in a statement. Albudaiwi called on the international community and the UN Security Council to fulfill their responsibilities and take effective measures to hold the Houthi militia accountable for its terrorist acts and prevent further threats. He stressed that failure to take firm action against attacks on civilians and civilian facilities would encourage the militia to carry out further attacks and increase risks to regional and international security and stability. The GCC chief reaffirmed the Gulf states' full and unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia and their support for all measures it takes to protect its security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, as well as the safety of its citizens and residents.

items.title: Arab, Islamic states hail UK, Australia sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements
items.title_zh: 阿拉伯和伊斯兰国家对英国和澳大利亚针对以色列非法定居点的制裁表示欢迎
items.summary: RIYADH — Ministers of foreign affairs of Saudi Arabia and several other Arab and Islamic countries welcomed the decisions of the governments of the United Kingdom and Australia to impose sanctions in response to illegal Israeli settlement activities in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including measures targeting companies involved in settlement construction. In a joint statement, they also welcome the United Kingdom’s decision to sanction an organization obstructing the delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza.The countries also include Jordan, Egypt, Pakistan, Indonesia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Niger, Palestine, Libya, Maldives, Türkiye, Kuwait, Algeria, Somalia and Oman. The ministers expressed support for all efforts to ensure accountability, including through appropriate international measures and the imposition of sanctions on entities and individuals responsible for settlement activities, including the E1 settlement plan, as well as those that support, facilitate or implement settlement expansion and annexation policies. The ministers renewed their strongest condemnation of Israel’s continued settlement policies in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, particularly the “E1” settlement plan and related settlement activities east of occupied East Jerusalem. They expressed the hope that this decision by the UK and Australia would encourage many in the international community to follow suit. The ministers consider these measures to be in line with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, including United Nations Security Council resolution 2334 of 2016, and the Advisory Opinion of the International Court of Justice of July 19, 2024, including the obligation of all states not to recognize as legal the situation arising from Israel’s unlawful occupation and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining the situation created by Israel’s occupation. In this regard, they reiterated their call for Israel to rescind all measures taken in connection with settlement activities and other measures aimed at altering the geographic and demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The ministers condemned the Israeli military escalation in Gaza and call for the full and immediate implementation of President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, to ensure security and stability, address the humanitarian situation, facilitate reconstruction and recovery, and lay the foundations for lasting peace. The ministers underscore that Gaza is an integral part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The ministers underscore that the only viable path to achieving a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace is the implementation of the two-State solution, through the realization of an independent, sovereign, contiguous, and viable Palestinian State, based on the June 4, 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions.

items.title: ‏Saudi Arabia ranks first globally in digital government services
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯在数字政务服务方面位居全球第一
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has achieved a historic global milestone by securing first place worldwide in the Online Services Index (OSI) and a position among the world’s top five countries in the United Nations E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This remarkable accomplishment marks the Kingdom’s attainment of its Saudi Vision 2030 target four years ahead of schedule. Saudi Arabia also ranked first globally in the Telecommunications Infrastructure Index (TII), the Participation and Engagement Index (PE), and the E-Government Infrastructure Index (EGI), while Riyadh ranked first in the Local Online Services Index (LOSI), according to the UN report, which assessed 194 countries.Minister of Communications and Information Technology and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Digital Government Authority Abdullah Alswaha extended his deepest gratitude and appreciation to Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for the unlimited support provided to the digital economy. He said that this global achievement is the result of Saudi Vision 2030, which has made technology and innovation key drivers of development, global competitiveness, and contributions to shaping the future.‎‏Digital Government Authority Governor Ahmed Alsuwaiyan expressed his profound gratitude and appreciation to the wise leadership for the continued support of the digital government ecosystem. He affirmed that this significant achievement reflects the maturity of digital transformation and the integration of efforts among government agencies, demonstrating Saudi Arabia’s progress in developing integrated, proactive, and human-centric digital government services. He pointed out that Saudi citizens are essential partners in this transformation and that their aspirations and needs have been, and continue to be, the primary driving force behind the development of government services and the utilization of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to enhance service quality and accessibility, thereby improving quality of life and delivering a more efficient and reliable digital experience.This achievement builds on the transformation journey undertaken by the digital government ecosystem since the establishment of the Digital Government Authority in 2021 to lead and regulate digital transformation through the development of policies, legislation, and standards, promoting the adoption of innovative and integrated digital solutions, and improving government spending efficiency. These efforts contribute to enhancing competitiveness, facilitating business activities, developing digital capabilities and skills, and advancing government services to higher levels of efficiency, quality, and proactivity.Since the Crown Prince launched Saudi Vision 2030 on April 25, 2016, the Vision has used the UN EGDI to measure progress toward its goal of placing Saudi Arabia among the world’s top five countries in digital government. Published every two years for 25 years and covering 194 countries, the index is one of the most prominent measures of government development worldwide. Saudi Arabia’s rise from 52nd in 2018 to fourth in 2026 reflects the scale of its digital government transformation and the Vision’s impact on government efficiency and the beneficiary experience.

items.title: Saudi, Syrian foreign ministers meet to discuss strengthening regional security
items.title_zh: 沙特、叙利亚外长会晤，讨论加强地区安全问题
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received Syrian Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Asaad Al-Shaibani at the ministry's headquarters in Riyadh on Thursday. During the meeting, they reviewed the fraternal relations between the two countries and their peoples, as well as ways to further enhance joint cooperation in various fields. They also discussed the latest regional developments and challenges facing the region. The ministers emphasized the importance of intensifying coordination and consultation regarding these issues to contribute to strengthening regional security and stability. Dr. Saud Al-Sati, undersecretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for political affairs, and Prince Musab Al-Farhan, advisor to the Minister of Foreign Affairs for political affairs, also attended the meeting.

items.title: Civil Defense urges caution as thunderstorms set to persist through Tuesday
items.title_zh: 民防部门敦促大家保持警惕，因为雷暴天气将持续到周二
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Directorate of Civil Defense urged people to exercise caution and remain in safe places amid forecast of thunderstorms continue hitting some regions of Saudi Arabia through next Tuesday. It called on the public to stay away from flood-prone areas and valleys, as well as to avoid swimming in them, and follow instructions of the concerned authorities. The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) said that the Makkah region will be affected by moderate rainfall accompanied by flash floods, hail, and downdraft winds stirring up dust and sand. It added that Jazan, Asir, and Al-Baha regions will be affected by moderate to heavy rainfall accompanied by flash floods, hail, and downdraft winds stirring up dust and sand.

items.title: Houthi attack damages King Abdullah Financial District tower in Riyadh; no injuries reported
items.title_zh: 胡塞武装的袭击损坏了利雅得的阿卜杜拉国王金融区大厦；据报道未造成人员受伤。
items.summary: RIYADH — A Houthi attack targeted a tower at the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) in Riyadh on Thursday, causing material damage to several floors and neighboring buildings but resulting in no injuries, Saudi Civil Defense announced.The official spokesperson for Civil Defense said emergency teams responded to the attack on Nov. 19, 2026, after a tower in the financial district was targeted by the Houthi militia.The attack caused material damage to several floors of the tower and nearby buildings, while no injuries were reported.The spokesperson condemned the targeting of civilian facilities, describing it as a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law.He said the attack reflected the danger posed by the Houthi militia's continued hostile actions.The spokesperson confirmed that the relevant authorities responded immediately to the incident and implemented all approved emergency measures and procedures to protect lives and property.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia strongly condemned the Houthi militia's continued attacks targeting civilian and economic facilities in Riyadh, including the latest attack that caused damage to the King Abdullah Financial District.In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom's strong condemnation and denunciation of the attacks against civilian facilities and infrastructure in the capital.The ministry reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's full and legitimate right to take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty, safeguard its national assets and protect the security and safety of citizens and residents."The Kingdom affirms its full and legitimate right to take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty, safeguard its national assets, and protect the security and safety of its citizens and residents," the ministry said.It stressed that Saudi Arabia would not tolerate any attack targeting its territory or national assets and would take the necessary measures in accordance with international law.The ministry also called on the international community, particularly the permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, to fulfill their responsibilities and implement relevant Security Council resolutions.It urged the international community to condemn the Houthi militia's attacks against Saudi Arabia, warning that the group poses a threat to regional and global security.

items.title: Saudi Arabia to introduce domestic minimum top-up tax for multinationals effective Jan. 1, 2027
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯将于2027年1月1日起对跨国公司征收国内最低补充税
items.summary: RIYADH — The Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) has announced that it will start implementing the domestic minimum top-up tax (DMTT) effective January 1, 2027. The tax applies to constituent entities of multinational enterprise (MNE) groups that have consolidated annual revenues of at least 750 million euro or its equivalent in Saudi riyal. The authority clarified that the tax will apply to entities meeting this revenue threshold according to the consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent entity in at least two of the four fiscal years preceding the year in which the tax is applied. The scope of application is limited to entities that meet the eligibility criteria within multinational groups and does not extend to all companies operating in Saudi Arabia. Accordingly, it excludes purely domestic companies that do not have branches outside Saudi Arabia or do not belong to a covered MNE group. The tax is based on the consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent entity in at least two of the four fiscal years preceding the fiscal year in which the tax applies, in a step aimed at protecting Saudi Arabia's tax rights and keeping pace with international tax developments. According to a press release issued by the ZATCA on Thursday, this tax comes within the framework of international trends aimed at establishing global minimum tax rules under Pillar Two, led by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the G20, thereby contributing to the protection of the Kingdom's tax rights on profits generated within its jurisdiction by the covered MNE groups. ZATCA explained that the DMTT allows for the collection of the top-up tax within the Kingdom on profits whenever the effective tax rate falls below the established global minimum threshold of 15 percent, in accordance with the relevant rules. This percentage refers to the minimum effective tax rate on profits and is not a rate levied on the total revenues of companies. The authority stated that the implementation of the DMTT aligns with international efforts aimed at enhancing tax fairness and ensuring that profits are subject to the global minimum tax in the countries where they are generated, supporting the protection of states' tax rights and enhancing the consistency of tax laws with international standards. ZATCA has invited targeted MNE entities and those seeking further information to reach out through its unified call center number 19993 (operating 24/7), the "Ask ZATCA" account on X @Zatca_care, via email at Info@zatca.gov.sa, or through the live chat feature on ZATCA's website ‏Zatca.gov.sa .

items.title: Saudi, Uzbek FMs discuss regional developments in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、乌兹别克斯坦外长在通话中讨论地区局势发展
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan has received on Thursday a phone call from Minister of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan Bakhtiyor Saidov. During the call, the ministers discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and ways to further improve them. They also reviewed the latest regional and international developments.

items.title: UK signs Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh
items.title_zh: 英国签署2030年利雅得世博会参展合同
items.summary: RIYADH — The United Kingdom has signed its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, confirming its place at one of the world’s largest global gatherings. The Participation Contract was signed by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Cabinet Member, Climate Envoy and Commissioner General of Expo 2030 Riyadh Adel Al-Jubeir; UK Minister for Trade Lord Sarwar; and CEO of Expo 2030 Riyadh Talal Al-Marri. The agreement constitutes a significant milestone in the United Kingdom’s journey towards Expo 2030 Riyadh, establishing the framework for the execution of its pavilion, programming and visitor experience. This latest agreement adds to a growing number of Participation Contract signings, reflecting increasing momentum behind Expo 2030 Riyadh and the value countries are placing on being part of it.The United Kingdom holds a distinctive place in the history of World Expos, having hosted the first World Expo in London in 1851. Conceived as an exhibition for “All Nations”, the Great Exhibition brought countries together to showcase human progress, innovation and industry, establishing a model of international exchange that has continued to shape World Expos ever since.In 2030, the United Kingdom will continue that tradition in Riyadh, bringing its ideas, expertise and innovation to a global gathering centered on the future. Through its pavilion and wider participation, the UK will contribute to the exchange of ideas and international collaboration at the heart of Expo 2030 Riyadh and its theme, Foresight for Tomorrow. Minister Adel Al-Jubeir commented: “The United Kingdom’s signing of its Participation Contract reinforces the spirit of international cooperation that lies at the heart of Expo 2030 Riyadh. Many of the opportunities and challenges before us transcend borders - the value of bringing nations together to exchange knowledge, deepen understanding and build new avenues for cooperation has never been more important.” UK Minister for Trade Anas Sarwar said: “I am delighted to confirm the UK’s participation at Expo 2030 Riyadh. As the hosts of the first World Expo in London in 1851, we understand the unique power of these events to bring people together, spark new ideas and forge lasting partnerships. As the UK and Saudi Arabia relationship continues to go from strength to strength, Expo 2030 Riyadh will create valuable opportunities for British businesses to build connections, explore new markets and develop partnerships that deliver lasting benefits for both our countries.” Commenting on the occasion, British Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Stephen Hitchen said: “The relationship between the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia has never been more important. As friends, partners and global collaborators, we are working together to unlock new opportunities in trade, investment, innovation, culture and education. As Saudi Arabia prepares to welcome the world to Riyadh in 2030, the United Kingdom is proud to support our Saudi partners in delivering what promises to be a truly remarkable World Expo.” The United Kingdom becomes part of a growing group of countries that have taken the next formal step in their participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh, with each Participation Contract bringing greater definition to the diverse experiences that nations will create for visitors in Riyadh in 2030. More than 185 Official Participants have now confirmed participation, with work progressing across pavilion planning, content and programming. Progress in international participation is being matched by progress on the Expo site itself. Across the six-million-square-metre site, major infrastructure works are advancing and key assets taking shape. Together, these developments are creating the foundations for participating countries to bring their presence to life, and for millions of visitors to experience Expo 2030 Riyadh in 2030. Held under the theme “Foresight for Tomorrow,” Expo 2030 Riyadh will take place from October 1, 2030 to March 31, 2031, bringing together countries and international organizations from around the world, with more than 42 million visits expected over six months. Through its five thematic areas - Technology, Planet, Humanity, Culture and Collaboration - the Expo will provide a global platform for nations to share their achievements and ambitions, explore solutions to shared challenges and inspire new possibilities for the future.

items.title: Electric bikes enhance 'Absher Travel for Visitors' service at land border crossings
items.title_zh: 电动自行车提升了陆地边境口岸的“Absher Travel for Visitors”服务
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Directorate of Passports is streamlining entry procedures for travelers at land border crossings by deploying electric bikes for passport security personnel to assist users of the "Absher Travel for Visitors" service. **media[2796780]**This service is available to citizens of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and visitors arriving in the Kingdom by land. The bikes allow passport security personnel to reach users faster so as to provide them with support. The directorate urged travelers to use the service via the Absher app. The service will become mandatory six months after October 26, 2026. It is designed to automate entry procedures for travelers and their vehicles by allowing them to complete travel requirements digitally before arriving at the border crossing across the Kingdom.
